367	## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done
368	
369	_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._
370	
371	Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
372	has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
373	`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.
374	
375	This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
376	and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.
377	
378	See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.
379	
380	### Four-layer model
381	
382	| Layer | Description |
383	|---|---|
384	| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
385	| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
386	| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
387	| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |
388	
389	### M7 task sequence
390	
391	| Task | Description | Depends on |
392	|---|---|---|
393	| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
394	| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
395	| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
396	| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
397	| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
398	| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
399	| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
400	| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
401	| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
402	| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
403	| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |
404	
405	### Permission policy design
406	
407	Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:
408	
409	```json
410	{
411	  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
412	  "default_decision": "ask",
413	  "reason": "External competition submission",
414	  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
415	  "audit_required": true
416	}
417	```
418	
419	Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
420	summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.
421	
422	Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
423	remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
424	change competition direction/objective.
425	
426	Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
427	drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.
428	
429	### Recommended directory layout
430	
431	```text
432	.kca/
433	  skills/
434	    run-milestone/SKILL.md
435	    triage-log/SKILL.md
436	    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
437	    review-pr/SKILL.md
438	  tools/tools.yaml
439	  permissions/
440	    default.yaml
441	    permissive-dev.yaml
442	    competition-runner.yaml
443	
444	tools/kca/
445	  kca.py
446	  commands/
447	    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
448	    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
449	  agent/
450	    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
451	    permission_policy.py  audit.py
452	```
453	
454	Exit criteria:
455	
456	- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
457	- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
458	- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
459	- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
460	- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
461	- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
462	- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
463	- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.

```markdown
## M14: goal-driven Kaggle workflow

_Filed 2026-06-09 from PR #44 follow-up. Five user-surfaced bullets become
GitHub issues #51 #52 #53 #54 #55 + M14 tasks T002 T003 T004 T005 T007.
Post-merge triage on 2026-06-09 also folded #7, #8, #62, #63 into the
plan (see task list below); #21 + #60 cross-referenced but deferred._

Goal: lift the platform from M10's single-shot, human-approved push into a
goal-tracking loop. Declare a target up front, fan out candidate experiments
locally, screen by holdout CV, push survivors to Kaggle under per-competition
concurrency limits, poll with adaptive cadence + batched status reads, write
LB scores back to the DB, and either iterate to the next batch or escalate to
a human when the idea well is dry.

Planned tasks:

- T000 [`arch:`] Goal-driven loop architecture + ADR-0020 + Discovery / Debate Gate
- T001 Migration 0011 (`goals` table + `competitions.max_*` + `submission_format` + `accelerators_allowed` + `experiment_runs.analysis.exploration_batch_id`) — absorbs #8 (competition-rules ingestion) + #7 (submission-format awareness)
- T002 `kca goal {init, show, update}` + `goal.md` workspace artefact (issue #51)
- T003 `kca explore {init, run, rank}` + local-screening fan-out (issue #52)
- T004 Per-competition concurrency enforcement + daily-budget gate + `cmd_push` credentials pre-check (issues #53, #62)
- T005 Smart polling: Fibonacci backoff QUEUED, stable RUNNING, batched `kernels list` (issue #54)
- T006 Idea-sourcing reader + `kca explore propose-next`

Supabase + `kca kaggle score` + `kca kaggle push --watch`); issues #51 #52
#53 #54 #55 promoted to `ai:ready` after triage.

Exit criteria:

- `kca goal init` writes a `goal.md` + DB row; reviewer gate surfaces
  `goal_remaining_delta`.
- `kca explore run` fans out N candidates locally and ranks them.
- `cmd_push` refuses cleanly when the per-competition concurrency or daily
  limit is reached.
- `_watch_kernel_until_terminal` classifies QUEUED vs RUNNING and adapts
  cadence; batched read kicks in for ≥ 2 tracked slugs.
- Stuck detector fires after N non-improving submissions and surfaces a
  `kaggle.exploration_stuck` decision in the Approval Inbox.
- T008's live end-to-end records ≥ 2 LB scores under the goal-driven loop,
  with at least one iteration step (initial batch → idea-source → next batch
  or escalation).
- `docs/m14-final-review.md` exists; PROJECT_STATE / README / milestones
  updated.

Out of scope for M14:

- A new Kaggle competition portfolio — `tpu-getting-started` is the
  default T008 surface unless T000 picks a smaller competition.
- CTF / Devpost / eval-suite integration of the goal/exploration/escalation
  primitives — M11 / M12 / M13 own those surfaces.
```

```markdown
# M14 — Loop Prompts

_Goal-driven Kaggle workflow: turn the platform from "one approved push" into
"set a goal, explore in parallel, push within Kaggle's rules, poll smartly,
escalate when stuck."_
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M10 exit confirmed (notebook-submission path validated;
see `docs/m10-final-review.md`). M11 (CTF), M12 (Devpost), M13 (eval
suite) are NOT prerequisites._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle / Anthropic
outside designated paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, per-milestone worktree
by default, secret denylist, Discovery / Debate Gate on `arch:` tasks)._

## M14 at a glance

M14 lifts the platform from M10's single-shot, human-approved push to a
**goal-driven Kaggle loop**: declare a target up front, fan out candidate
experiments locally, screen them by holdout CV, push the survivors to Kaggle
under per-competition concurrency limits, poll their kernel runs with adaptive
cadence + batched status reads, write LB scores back to the DB, and either
(a) iterate to the next batch when below goal, or (b) escalate to a human when
the idea well is dry.

The five user-surfaced bullets from PR #44 each become a numbered task in this
milestone, tracked by an `ai:triage` GitHub issue:

| Bullet / topic | Issue | M14 task |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting at start of competition | #51 | T002 |
| Parallel exploration with local GPU screening | #52 | T003 |
| Multi-push concurrency within Kaggle rules | #53 | T004 |
| Smart polling: backoff + batched status reads | #54 | T005 |
| Human-in-the-loop escalation when stuck | #55 | T007 |
| Competition-rules ingestion (quota / accelerators / internet / deadlines / format) | #8 (parent), #7 (submission-format sub-task) | T001 |
| `cmd_push` missing `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` pre-check (M13 deviation) | #62 | T004 |
| Gate PRs on eval score-delta (per `docs/m13-final-review.md` follow-up 3) | #63 | T009 |

Related but **not** in M14's deliverable surface (cross-referenced from
the relevant Loop Prompt read-lists for context, no work scheduled):

- #21 — per-account quota pool. M14 ships the **single-account** primitive
  (T004); the multi-account variant is M15+.
- #60 — `approved_by_user_id` FK on `human_decisions`. M14-T007 inserts
  new rows of this type; the FK hardening is a separate audit task.

Direct entry into M14 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M10 is merged on `main` (`docs/m10-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- Cloud Supabase is the active DB (M10 follow-up PR #44 merged on `main`),
  with M10's `submissions` / `experiment_runs` / `competitions` rows reachable.
  M14's new tables sit alongside them.
- The `kca kaggle push --watch` auto-poll feature (M10 follow-up) is on `main`.
  M14-T005 replaces its naive cadence with the smart-polling logic but reuses
  the same watcher entry point.
- Issues #51 #52 #53 #54 #55 have been triaged to `ai:ready` (each starts
  `ai:triage`; promotion requires explicit acceptance criteria sign-off).

### What's in scope

| Idea-sourcing reader (forum / public kernels / arxiv) → `next_candidates.yaml` | `tools/kca/research.py` extension + new `kca explore propose-next` | T006 |

### What's NOT in scope

- **A new ML breakthrough.** M14 is a workflow milestone; the only modelling
```

```
#### KCA autonomous submission strategy

KCA targets submission approximately 2 hours before the daily roll-over (00:00 UTC). Apply this strategy per competition day:

| Scenario | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exactly 1 candidate beats the current best score | Submit that candidate; use remaining daily slots for exploration near the baseline |
| 2 | No candidate beats the current best score | Do not waste the daily balance; use all slots for exploration near the baseline |
| 3 | Multiple candidates beat best score, competition open (≥ closing threshold) | Submit the best N (up to daily limit); queue remainder for the next day |
| 4 | Multiple candidates beat best score, competition closing soon (< closing threshold) | Ask human to decide which candidates to promote |

Closing threshold = `competition_period × 0.1` (default: 5 days for a 50-day competition); configurable per project.

### CTF

- Work only on explicitly authorized CTF challenges, local labs, or sandbox targets provided by the human.
- Do not attack third-party systems, scan public IP ranges, exfiltrate real credentials, deploy malware, or persist access.
- When a technique could be dual-use, keep execution inside the provided challenge/container and write explanations as educational competition notes.

## Default workflow
```

```python
"""Sync reviewer agent (M6-T004 / ADR-0012).

When the primary worker is about to call a high-stakes operation
(`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
`delete_artifact`), the reviewer reads the job's event trail and final
plan, calls a reviewer model via LiteLLM, and returns a verdict
(`approve` | `reject` | `abstain`). Sync-only for M6.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

    "kaggle_submit",
    "supabase_migrate",
    "git_force_push",
    "dataset_upload",
    "delete_artifact",

    # deny-default authority for these; the hook layer
    # (.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py) acts as a secondary defense for known-bad
    # paths/hosts even before the reviewer fires. An httpx-level interceptor
    # is out of scope for M11 (filed as a follow-up).
    "challenge_run",
    "flag_submit",
    "network_egress",
)

# Flag-substring sentinels we MUST NOT render into the reviewer prompt for
# the flag_submit op. Kept narrow on purpose: the worker is expected to pass
# the flag value under the `tool_input["flag"]` key.
_FLAG_INPUT_KEYS = ("flag", "flag_value", "submission")


@dataclass
class ReviewRequest:
    job_id: str
    target_op: str
    tool_name: str
    tool_input: dict
    final_message: str | None = None
    event_trail: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class ReviewVerdict:
    verdict: str
    rationale: str
    evidence: dict
    cost_usd: float
    reviewer_model: str


_REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a sync reviewer for a Kaggle/CTF code agent. The primary "
    "worker is about to invoke a high-stakes operation. Read the job "
    "context below and decide whether the call should proceed.\n\n"
    "Return STRICT JSON only (no prose, no markdown), exactly: "
    '{"verdict": "approve|reject|abstain", '
    '"rationale": "<one paragraph>", '
    '"evidence": {"key_signals": [...]}}\n\n'
    "Use approve when the plan and tool input clearly match the stated "
    "task and contain no destructive surprise. Use reject when the call "
    "would touch the wrong data, push the wrong file, leak secrets, or "
    "violate competition/CTF rules. Use abstain when context is too thin "
    "to decide; a human will be paged."
)


def _trim_event_trail(events: list[dict], max_events: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    """Keep at most the most-recent max_events events, drop bulky fields."""
    if len(events) > max_events:
        events = events[-max_events:]
    pruned: list[dict] = []
    for ev in events:
        pruned.append(
            {
                "event_type": ev.get("event_type"),
                "turn_number": ev.get("turn_number"),
                "event_data": ev.get("event_data"),
            }
        )
    return pruned


_EVENT_TRAIL_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD = 8 * 1024  # 8 KB
```

````
# ADR-0020: Goal-driven Kaggle loop

## Status

Proposed (M14, 2026-06-10). Subject to confirmation on the M14
proposal issue after the Discovery / Debate Gate transcripts at
`docs/evidence/m14/T000/discovery/` have been reviewed, and after the
five human decisions in `docs/m14-loop-prompts.md` §"Human decisions
needed before starting M14" are pinned.

Supersedes nothing; builds on ADR-0006 (configurable approval gates)
and ADR-0010 (per-job-type model routing). Cross-references ADR-0008
(artifact storage local-first) and ADR-0018 (generalized competition
type).

## Context

M0–M10 shipped the platform's single-shot Kaggle path: register a
competition, build a baseline notebook, pass the `kernel_push` reviewer
gate, push **one** human-approved kernel, watch it to terminal, record
the submission. M10's final review (`docs/m10-final-review.md`)
confirmed the loop runs end-to-end but also surfaced its limits: push #1
stalled QUEUED ~66 min and never ran; the watcher used a fixed 60 s
cadence; there was no notion of a *target* the loop was working toward,
no parallel exploration, no concurrency accounting, and no automatic
escalation when progress stalled.

M14 lifts the platform from "one approved push" to a **goal-driven
loop**: declare a target up front, fan out candidate experiments
locally, screen them by holdout CV, push the survivors to Kaggle under
per-competition concurrency limits, poll with adaptive cadence + batched
status reads, write LB scores back to the DB, and either iterate to the
next batch or escalate to a human when the idea well is dry.

This ADR pins the architectural decisions; the companion
[`docs/architecture/goal-driven-kaggle-loop.md`](../architecture/goal-driven-kaggle-loop.md)
carries the ASCII data-flow, table layouts, state-machine diagram, and
payload shapes the decisions imply. The ten task specs
`docs/tasks/M14-T000-*.md` … `M14-T009-*.md` implement it.

Inputs that shape this ADR:

- ADR-0006 (configurable approval gates) — the new per-batch push
  budget and the `kaggle.exploration_stuck` decision_type follow the
  same per-project / per-competition / per-job override pattern.
- ADR-0010 (per-job-type model routing) — `propose-next` (T006) reuses
  `src/worker/routing.py`'s `research` route; no parallel router.
- M10-T004 / M10-T007 — the `kernels output`-size terminal detection
  fallback, the QUEUED-stall failure mode, and the audit-grep sentinel
  ("0 lines reach `kaggle kernels push` from any non-approved process")
  are all preserved, not regressed.
- Discovery / Debate Gate (M9.4) — the three transcripts at
  `docs/evidence/m14/T000/discovery/` (legacy-archaeologist SKIP-NOTE,
  requirements-skeptic, design-red-team) informed every decision below.
  Where the red-team flagged an `open_disagreement`, the resolution is
  noted inline under the relevant decision.

## Decision

The goal-driven loop ships as an eight-decision package.

### 1. `goal.md` schema — score-primary, rank-secondary, with explicit exit_strategy

A goal is declared per competition. The DB `goals` row is authoritative;
`experiments/<comp>/goal.md` is a human-readable mirror for git history.
The schema:

```yaml
# experiments/<comp>/goal.md  (front-matter mirror of the goals row)
competition: tpu-getting-started
target_lb_score: 0.85          # primary — absolute, metric-direction aware
target_lb_rank: 30             # secondary — percentile or absolute rank; nullable
target_rank_kind: percentile   # 'percentile' | 'absolute'; only meaningful with target_lb_rank
deadline: 2026-07-01           # nullable; the competition deadline or an earlier self-imposed one
exit_strategy: first_reached   # 'first_reached' | 'all_required' | 'score_only' | 'rank_only'
max_total_pushes: 20           # hard ceiling on real pushes across the whole exercise
stuck_threshold: 3             # N consecutive non-improving submissions before escalation
status: active                 # 'active' | 'reached' | 'closed' | 'abandoned'
```

- **`target_lb_score` is the primary goal type.** Resolving the
  red-team / skeptic concern that `target_lb_rank` requires a live
  leaderboard read on every tick: rank is **secondary and best-effort**.
  The loop's primary stop signal is the absolute score, which is
  recorded on `submissions.public_lb_score` and evaluable offline. Rank
  is refreshed only on a terminal LB write (not every poll tick) and may
  be NULL if the rank read fails — a NULL rank never blocks the loop.
- `exit_strategy` makes the goal-met predicate explicit:
  `first_reached` (score OR rank, default), `all_required` (score AND
  rank), `score_only`, `rank_only`. This pins skeptic explicit_unknown
  on `target_lb_rank` primacy (human decision 1).
- `max_total_pushes` (default 20) is the hard ceiling enforced by T008's
  loop, independent of the per-day budget.
- `stuck_threshold` (default 3) is the T007 detector's N (human
  decision 4).

### 2. `goals` table + FKs — new table, FK from `submissions`, no `experiment_runs` schema change in this decision
````

```
## Scope
1. `tools/kca/goal.py` exporting `add_parsers(subparsers)`, registered
   from `tools/kca/kca.py`:
   - `kca goal init --competition <slug> --target-lb-score <f>
     [--target-lb-rank <int>] [--target-rank-kind percentile|absolute]
     [--deadline yyyy-mm-dd] [--exit-strategy first_reached|all_required|score_only|rank_only]
     [--max-total-pushes 20] [--stuck-threshold 3] [--json]` — creates
     the `goals` row (refuses if an active goal exists) and writes
     `experiments/<comp>/goal.md`.
   - `kca goal show --competition <slug> [--json]` — reads the active
     goal row; prints score/rank targets, exit_strategy, status,
     `goal_remaining_delta` (best current LB vs target).
   - `kca goal update --competition <slug> [--target-lb-score ...]
     [--deadline ...] [--stuck-threshold ...] [--close --reason <text>] [--json]`
     — updates fields or closes the goal; rewrites `goal.md`.
2. `goal.md` writer — YAML front-matter mirror of the row (ADR-0020 §1)
   plus a human-readable body; idempotent rewrite on update.
3. Reviewer-gate integration: the `kernel_push` gate prompt surfaces
   `goal_remaining_delta` so the approver sees how far the push could
   move the goal. (Read-only enrichment; does not change gate logic.)

## Non-goals
- No exploration / batch surface (T003).
- No concurrency / push changes (T004).
- No real Kaggle calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- `kca goal --help` lists `init`, `show`, `update`.
```

```python
"""FastAPI action service for the M8 Decision Gate UI.

The browser never holds a service-role Supabase key. It posts to
``/decision/<id>/approve|reject|ask-improve``; this service re-uses the
existing ``tools/kca/decisions.py`` functions and ``tools/kca/db.py`` writes
so the M7 permission policy stays authoritative.

Auth: a shared token in ``KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN``. Requests must include the
matching ``X-Decision-Api-Token`` header. Multi-user auth lands in M9+.

Testing: pass a ``decisions_module`` override (e.g. via dependency injection)
to swap in a mocked DB layer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import os
from typing import Callable, Optional

from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


TOKEN_ENV = "KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN"


class ApproveBody(BaseModel):
    reason: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)


class RejectBody(BaseModel):
    reason: str = Field(..., min_length=8, max_length=2000)


class AskImproveBody(BaseModel):
    feedback: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=4000)
    metric_target: Optional[str] = None


def _check_token(provided: Optional[str]) -> None:
    expected = os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV, "")
    if not expected:
        # If the server has no token configured, accept any (local dev only).
        return
    if not provided or not hmac.compare_digest(provided, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="invalid token")


def make_app(
    decisions_module: Optional[object] = None,
    audit_logger: Optional[Callable] = None,
    submission_pack_provider: Optional[Callable[[str], dict]] = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Construct the FastAPI app.

    ``decisions_module`` exposes ``get_decision``, ``resolve_decision``, and
    ``append_job_event``. Tests pass a fake module to avoid touching Supabase.

    ``submission_pack_provider`` is the optional READ_ONLY hook for the
    ``GET /runs/{run_id}/submission_pack`` endpoint (M12-T005). When
    omitted, the endpoint resolves the run -> competition -> slug +
    submission_format via the real DB layer and shells out to
    ``tools/kca/submission_checklist.build_checklist`` so the UI sees the
    same checklist the worker tool sees. Tests inject a deterministic
    in-memory provider to avoid touching Supabase / the filesystem.
    """
    app = FastAPI(title="kca decision_api", version="0.1.0")

    def _resolve_db():
        if decisions_module is not None:
            return decisions_module
        import sys
        from pathlib import Path

        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tools" / "kca"))
        import db as _db  # type: ignore

        return _db

    def _audit(*, decision: str, decision_id: str, reason: Optional[str]) -> None:
        if audit_logger is not None:
            audit_logger(
                decision=decision, decision_id=decision_id, reason=reason or ""
            )
            return
        try:
            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore

            log_policy_decision(
                tool="decision_api",
                operation=f"decision_{decision}",
                decision="allow",
                policy_profile="default",
                args={"decision_id": decision_id, "reason_len": len(reason or "")},
            )
        except Exception:
            pass
```

````
# Goal-driven Kaggle loop — architecture

Status: M14 (2026-06-10). Companion to
[`ADR-0020`](../adr/0020-goal-driven-kaggle-loop.md). T000 lands this
doc + the ADR; T001 lands migration 0011 + DB helpers; T002–T007 fill
the CLI + worker surfaces; T008 runs the live end-to-end; T009 is the
milestone close.

## Goals (recap)

Turn the platform from "one approved push" (M10) into "set a goal,
explore in parallel, push within Kaggle's rules, poll smartly, escalate
when stuck." Score-primary goals; rank best-effort. One real Kaggle
write surface (T008), per-batch human-approved, under a courtesy
concurrency + daily-budget gate. Never call real Kaggle from any
non-approved process (M10-T007 audit-grep sentinel inherited).

## ASCII data-flow

```
                 +----------------------------+
                 | experiments/<comp>/goal.md |  (human-readable mirror)
                 +-------------+--------------+
                               | kca goal init/update
                               v
   +-----------+        +------+------+        search-space.yaml
   | competit- |<--FK---|   goals     |        +----------------+
   |   ions    |        | (1 active   |        | axes: backbone |
   | max_*,    |        |  per comp)  |        |       img_size |
   | rules,    |        +------+------+        |       epochs   |
   | format    |               |              +-------+--------+
   +-----------+               | goal_id              | kca explore init
                               |                      v
                               |          +-----------+-----------+
                               |          | exploration batch     |
                               |          | (uuid; batch.yaml)    |
                               |          | init->fanout->screen  |
                               |          |   ->rank->promote      |
                               |          +-----------+-----------+
                               |                      | one experiment_runs
                               |                      | row per cell
                               |                      v
                               |          +-----------+-----------+
                               |          | experiment_runs       |
                               |          |  metrics jsonb:       |  <- holdout_accuracy,
                               |          |    (metric values)    |     macro_f1, train_seconds
                               |          |  analysis_jsonb (NEW): |  <- exploration_batch_id,
                               |          |   loop metadata        |     parent_run_id,
                               |          +-----------+-----------+     queue_time_seconds,
                               |                      | kca explore rank running_time_seconds,
                               |                      | (top-K qualify)  escalation_id
                               |                      v
                               |          +-----------+-----------+
                               |          | promote -> cmd_push   |
                               |          +-----------+-----------+
                               |                      | (1) creds pre-check
                               |                      | (2) concurrency gate
                               |                      | (3) daily-budget gate
                               |                      | (4) per-batch approval

## Table layouts

### `goals` (new — migration 0011)

| Column | Type | Nullable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid pk | no | `gen_random_uuid()` |
| `competition_id` | uuid | no | FK → `competitions(id)` on delete cascade |
| `target_lb_score` | numeric(10,6) | yes | primary goal type |
| `target_lb_rank` | int | yes | secondary, best-effort |
| `target_rank_kind` | text | yes | check in (`percentile`,`absolute`) |
| `deadline` | timestamptz | yes | competition or self-imposed |
| `exit_strategy` | text | no | check in (`first_reached`,`all_required`,`score_only`,`rank_only`) |
| `max_total_pushes` | int | no | default 20 |
| `stuck_threshold` | int | no | default 3 |
| `status` | text | no | check in (`active`,`reached`,`closed`,`abandoned`); default `active` |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | no | default `now()` |
| `closed_at` | timestamptz | yes | |
| `closed_reason` | text | yes | |

Indexes: partial unique `(competition_id) where status='active'`;
`(competition_id)`.

| `internet_allowed` | boolean | yes | |
````

```python
"""Worker tool definitions and executor.

TOOL_SCHEMAS uses OpenAI tool schema format (LiteLLM-compatible for all providers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool schemas (OpenAI format)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "read_file",
            "description": "Read a file relative to the workspace root.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Path relative to workspace root",
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "write_file",
            "description": "Write content to a file in the workspace.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "content": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "content"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "edit_file",
            "description": "Replace the first occurrence of old_string with new_string in a file.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "old_string": {"type": "string"},
                    "new_string": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "old_string", "new_string"],
            },
        },

            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",

                    "command": {"type": "string"},
                    "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 60},
                },
                "required": ["command"],
            },
        },

    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "grep_workspace",
            "description": "Search for a pattern in the workspace files.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "pattern": {"type": "string"},
                    "path": {"type": "string", "default": "."},
                },
                "required": ["pattern"],
            },
        },
    },
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Side-effect classification helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER = ["READ_ONLY", "LOCAL_WRITE", "REMOTE_WRITE", "SUBMISSION"]

# Hard-deny patterns for run_bash (regardless of policy).
_HARD_DENY_PATTERNS = [
    "sudo *",
    "rm -rf*",
    "git push*",
    "kaggle submit*",
]
_HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS = [".."]


def _side_effect_ge(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if side-effect a >= b in severity."""
    try:
        return _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(a) >= _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(b)
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _bash_side_effect(command: str) -> str:
    """Classify the side-effect level of a bash command."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle submit*", "kca kaggle push*", "kca kaggle upload*"]
    ):
        return "SUBMISSION"
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle *", "kca run *", "python *", "pytest *"]
    ):
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"
    return "LOCAL_WRITE"


def _is_bash_allowed(command: str, policy: JobPolicy) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (allowed, reason). Hard-deny takes priority over policy."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    for sub in _HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS:
        if sub in cmd:
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in _HARD_DENY_PATTERNS:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in policy.allowed_tool_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return True, ""
    return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ApprovalRequired exception
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
    """Raised when a tool call exceeds policy.max_side_effect."""

    def __init__(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, side_effect: str):
        self.tool_name = tool_name
        self.tool_input = tool_input
        self.side_effect = side_effect
        super().__init__(f"{tool_name} requires approval (side_effect={side_effect})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ToolExecutor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ToolExecutor:
    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, policy: JobPolicy):
        self.workspace = workspace.resolve()
        self.policy = policy

    def _guard_path(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path | None, str | None]:
        """Resolve path within workspace. Return (resolved, None) or (None, error)."""
        target = (self.workspace / path).resolve()
        if not str(target).startswith(str(self.workspace)):
            return None, f"path traversal rejected: {path}"
        return target, None

    def execute(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        # Determine side effect and check approval gate.
        se = self._classify_side_effect(tool_name, tool_input)
        if (
            _side_effect_ge(se, self.policy.max_side_effect)
            and se != self.policy.max_side_effect
        ):
            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, se)

        if tool_name == "read_file":
            return self._read_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "write_file":
            return self._write_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "edit_file":
            return self._edit_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "run_bash":
            return self._run_bash(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "grep_workspace":
            return self._grep_workspace(tool_input)
        else:
            return f"unknown tool: {tool_name}"

    def _classify_side_effect(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        if tool_name in ("read_file", "grep_workspace"):
            return "READ_ONLY"
        if tool_name in ("write_file", "edit_file"):
            return "LOCAL_WRITE"
        if tool_name == "run_bash":
            return _bash_side_effect(tool_input.get("command", ""))
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"

    def _read_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            return target.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception as e:
            return f"read_file error: {e}"

    def _write_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(inp["content"])
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"write_file error: {e}"

    def _edit_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            text = target.read_text(errors="replace")
            old = inp["old_string"]
            new = inp["new_string"]
            if old not in text:
                return f"edit_file error: old_string not found in {inp['path']}"
            target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"edit_file error: {e}"

    def _run_bash(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        command = inp.get("command", "")
        timeout_s = int(inp.get("timeout_s", 60))
        allowed, reason = _is_bash_allowed(command, self.policy)
        if not allowed:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": reason, "exit_code": 126})
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                command,
                shell=True,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=timeout_s,
                cwd=str(self.workspace),
            )
            return json.dumps(
                {
                    "stdout": proc.stdout,
                    "stderr": proc.stderr,
                    "exit_code": proc.returncode,
                }
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": "timeout", "exit_code": 124})
        except Exception as e:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": str(e), "exit_code": 1})

    def _grep_workspace(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        pattern = inp.get("pattern", "")
        search_path = inp.get("path", ".")
        target, err = self._guard_path(search_path)
        if err:
            return err
        results = []
        try:
            for p in sorted(target.rglob("*")):
                if not p.is_file():
                    continue
                try:
                    for i, line in enumerate(
                        p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
                    ):
                        if pattern.lower() in line.lower():
                            results.append(
                                {
                                    "file": str(p.relative_to(self.workspace)),
                                    "line_number": i,
                                    "line": line,
                                }
                            )
                except Exception:
                    continue
        except Exception as e:
            return f"grep_workspace error: {e}"
        return json.dumps(results)
```

```python
"""AgentWorker — agentic tool loop powered by LiteLLM (ADR-0004)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
import types
from pathlib import Path

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy, WorkerResult
from src.worker.tools import TOOL_SCHEMAS, ToolExecutor, ApprovalRequired
from src.worker.budget import BudgetTracker


class PolicyViolation(Exception):
    """Raised when an M8 ``tool_decisions[tool]`` resolves to ``deny``.

    Distinct from :class:`ApprovalRequired` so the worker can mark the job
    failed (and never side-effect) instead of pausing for a human.
    """

    def __init__(self, tool_name: str, decision: str = "deny"):
        self.tool_name = tool_name
        self.decision = decision
        super().__init__(f"{tool_name} denied by policy ({decision})")


# M11 (ADR-0017): map tool_name to reviewer target_op for the new CTF ops.
# The default identity mapping (target_op == tool_name) covers M6/M9/M10 ops
# (kaggle_submit, kernel_push, supabase_migrate, ...). The mapping below is
# only consulted for synthetic / wrapper tools whose tool_name doesn't match
# the operation in the policy YAMLs. Each entry must correspond to an
# operation row in .kca/permissions/*.yaml.
_TOOL_TO_TARGET_OP: dict[str, str] = {
    # `kca ctf solver run` invocation surfaces as a `challenge_run` op.
    "kca_ctf_solver_run": "challenge_run",
    "ctf_solver_run": "challenge_run",
    "challenge_run": "challenge_run",
    # `kca ctf flag submit` invocation surfaces as a `flag_submit` op.
    "kca_ctf_flag_submit": "flag_submit",
    "ctf_flag_submit": "flag_submit",
    "flag_submit": "flag_submit",
    # Worker-issued HTTP egress that doesn't match the ctf_scopes.target_urls
    # union surfaces as a `network_egress` op.
    "http_request": "network_egress",
    "network_egress": "network_egress",
}


def _resolve_target_op(tool_name: str) -> str:
    """Return the reviewer target_op string for the given tool_name.

    For unknown tools, target_op == tool_name (the M6/M9/M10 contract).
    """
    return _TOOL_TO_TARGET_OP.get(tool_name, tool_name)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mock LiteLLM client for dry_run tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _make_usage(prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int):
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        prompt_tokens=prompt_tokens,
        completion_tokens=completion_tokens,
    )


def _make_tool_calls_response(
    tool_name: str,
    tool_input: dict,
    prompt_tokens: int = 50,
    completion_tokens: int = 20,
):
    tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
        id=f"call_{tool_name}",
        type="function",
        function=types.SimpleNamespace(
            name=tool_name,
            arguments=json.dumps(tool_input),
        ),
    )
    msg = types.SimpleNamespace(
        content=None,
        tool_calls=[tc],
    )
    choice = types.SimpleNamespace(
        message=msg,
        finish_reason="tool_calls",
    )
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        choices=[choice],
        usage=_make_usage(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens),
    )


def _make_stop_response(
    text: str, prompt_tokens: int = 30, completion_tokens: int = 10
):
    msg = types.SimpleNamespace(
        content=text,
        tool_calls=None,
    )
    choice = types.SimpleNamespace(
        message=msg,
        finish_reason="stop",
    )
    return types.SimpleNamespace(
        choices=[choice],
        usage=_make_usage(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens),
    )


class MockLiteLLMClient:
    """Deterministic LiteLLM mock. Never calls any real API."""

    def __init__(self, scenario: str = "two_turns"):
        self._turn = 0
        self._scenario = scenario

    def completion(self, **kwargs) -> object:
        self._turn += 1
        if self._scenario == "two_turns":
            if self._turn == 1:
                return _make_tool_calls_response(
                    "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 50, 20
                )
            return _make_stop_response("dry run complete", 30, 10)
        if self._scenario == "infinite_tool":
            return _make_tool_calls_response(
                "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 100, 50
            )
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scenario: {self._scenario}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AgentWorker
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AgentWorker:
    """Competition agent worker using LiteLLM as the provider layer (ADR-0004)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        job_id: str,
        prompt: str,
        policy: JobPolicy,
        workspace: Path,
        db_url: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        resume_state: dict | None = None,
    ):
        self.job_id = job_id
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.policy = policy
        self.workspace = Path(workspace)
        self.db_url = db_url
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        # Optional resume state: {turns_used, cost_usd, last_msg, allow_once}
        self.resume_state = resume_state or {}
        # model kwarg overrides policy.model when given
        if model is not None:
            self.policy = JobPolicy(
                max_turns=policy.max_turns,
                max_cost_usd=policy.max_cost_usd,
                max_runtime_s=policy.max_runtime_s,
                allowed_tool_patterns=policy.allowed_tool_patterns,
                model=model,
                temperature=policy.temperature,
                top_p=policy.top_p,
                min_p=policy.min_p,
                approval_gates=policy.approval_gates,
                max_side_effect=policy.max_side_effect,
                skill_name=getattr(policy, "skill_name", None),
                policy_profile=getattr(policy, "policy_profile", "default"),
                mode=getattr(policy, "mode", "default"),
                tool_decisions=dict(getattr(policy, "tool_decisions", {})),
            )
        # Allow test code to override the mock scenario or inject a client directly.
        self._mock_scenario: str = "two_turns"
        self._mock_client: MockLiteLLMClient | None = None

    def run(self) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        # Only tag spans with a job_id when we know that row exists in the DB
        # (otherwise the Supabase exporter trips on the agent_jobs FK).
        tracer_job_id = self.job_id if self.db_url else None
        tracer = _otel.build_tracer(job_id=tracer_job_id)
        if tracer.is_enabled():
            job_span = _otel.start_job_span(tracer, self.job_id, self.prompt)
            try:
                if self.db_url and self.job_id:
                    self._safe_set_job_trace(tracer.trace_id, job_span.span_id)
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            job_span = None
        try:
            return self._run_inner(tracer)
        finally:
            if job_span is not None:
                job_span.end()

    def _safe_set_job_trace(self, trace_id: str, root_span_id: str) -> None:
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.set_job_trace(self.job_id, trace_id, root_span_id)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _run_inner(self, tracer) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        if self._mock_client is not None:
            client = self._mock_client
        elif self.dry_run:
            client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario=self._mock_scenario)
        else:
            client = None
        budget = BudgetTracker(self.policy, model=self.policy.model)
        # Seed from resume_state so cumulative turns/cost roll forward.
        if self.resume_state:
            budget.turns = int(self.resume_state.get("turns_used") or 0)
            budget.cost_usd = float(self.resume_state.get("cost_usd") or 0.0)
        executor = ToolExecutor(self.workspace, self.policy)
        # One-shot allowlist for the paused tool_input from a prior pause.
        allow_once = (self.resume_state or {}).get("allow_once") or None
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": self.prompt}]
        start = time.monotonic()

        while True:
            # 1. Pre-turn budget check
            stop_reason = budget.check_limits()
            if stop_reason:
                self._update_status("failed", error=stop_reason, budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="budget_stop",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message="",
                    stop_reason=stop_reason,
                )

            # 2. LiteLLM call (OpenAI format for all providers)
            extra: dict = (
                {} if self.policy.min_p is None else {"min_p": self.policy.min_p}
            )
            with _otel.with_turn_span(tracer, budget.turns + 1) as _turn_span:
                if client is not None:
                    response = client.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                else:
                    import litellm

                    response = litellm.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                if _turn_span is not None:
                    _turn_span.set_attribute("model", self.policy.model)
                    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
                    if usage is not None:
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "prompt_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                        )
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "completion_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                        )

            # 3. Record turn cost
            budget.record_turn(response)
            msg = response.choices[0].message
            finish_reason = response.choices[0].finish_reason

            self._append_event(
                "turn_start",
                budget.turns,
                input_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                output_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                event_data={"finish_reason": finish_reason},
            )

            # 4. stop → job done
            if finish_reason == "stop":
                final_text = msg.content or ""
                self._update_status("succeeded", budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="done",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message=final_text,
                    stop_reason="end_turn",
                )

            # 5. tool_calls → execute each tool
            if finish_reason == "tool_calls":
                tool_calls = msg.tool_calls or []
                # Append assistant turn with tool_calls (OpenAI message format)
                messages.append(
                    {
                        "role": "assistant",
                        "content": msg.content,
                        "tool_calls": [
                            {
                                "id": tc.id,
                                "type": "function",
                                "function": {
                                    "name": tc.function.name,
                                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
                                },
                            }
                            for tc in tool_calls
                        ],
                    }
                )
                for tc in tool_calls:
                    tool_input = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
                    self._append_event(
                        "tool_call",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={"tool": tc.function.name, "input": tool_input},
                    )
                    try:
                        with _otel.with_tool_span(tracer, tc.function.name, tool_input):
                            result_content = self._tool_call(
                                executor, tc.function.name, tool_input
                            )
                    except PolicyViolation as exc:
                        # M8 hard-deny path: log + fail the job, no side effects.
                        self._update_status(
                            "failed",
                            error=f"policy_violation: {exc}",
                            budget=budget,
                        )
                        return WorkerResult(
                            status="failed",
                            turns_used=budget.turns,
                            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                            final_message="",
                            stop_reason="policy_violation",
                        )
                    except ApprovalRequired as exc:
                        # One-shot resume allowance: bypass the matching gate
                        # exactly once after `kca decisions approve`.
                        if allow_once and (
                            allow_once.get("operation") == exc.tool_name
                            or allow_once.get("operation") == "tool_approval"
                        ):
                            allow_once = None  # consume
                            # Recurse into the actual tool with policy bypass
                            # by temporarily relaxing max_side_effect for this
                            # one call.
                            saved = executor.policy.max_side_effect
                            executor.policy.max_side_effect = "SUBMISSION"
                            try:
                                result_content = executor.execute(
                                    tc.function.name, tool_input
                                )
                            finally:
                                executor.policy.max_side_effect = saved
                        else:
                            return self._handle_approval_required(exc, budget, start)

                    self._append_event(
                        "tool_result",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={
                            "tool": tc.function.name,
                            "result_preview": str(result_content)[:200],
                        },
                    )
                    messages.append(
                        {
                            "role": "tool",
                            "tool_call_id": tc.id,
                            "content": str(result_content),
                        }
                    )
                continue

            # 6. Unexpected finish_reason
            self._update_status(
                "failed",
                error=f"unexpected finish_reason={finish_reason}",
                budget=budget,
            )
            return WorkerResult(
                status="failed",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="",
                stop_reason="unexpected",
            )

    def _tool_call(
        self, executor: "ToolExecutor", tool_name: str, tool_input: dict
    ) -> str:
        """M8 tool dispatch with ToolSpec + JobPolicy enforcement.

        Resolution order:
          1. JobPolicy.tool_decisions[tool_name]: "deny" → PolicyViolation;
             "ask" → ApprovalRequired (pauses job, records human_decisions);
             "allow" or unset → fall through.
          2. ToolSpec.sandbox: "unsandboxed" requires the policy decision to
             be "allow"; "isolated_workspace" requires cwd to be the job
             workspace.
          3. ToolSpec.timeout_s wraps the call so a hung tool cannot exceed
             the declared budget (applies to ``run_bash`` and other
             subprocess-shaped tools; in-process tools observe it via a best
             effort signal-based deadline).
          4. Every decision is audited via
             ``tools.kca.agent.audit.log_policy_decision`` so the
             ``agent_tool_audit`` table records the outcome.
        """
        decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(tool_name)
        spec = self._tool_spec(tool_name)
        self._audit_tool_decision(
            tool_name=tool_name,
            decision=decision or "allow",
            spec=spec,
            tool_input=tool_input,
        )

        if decision == "deny":
            raise PolicyViolation(tool_name, decision="deny")
        if decision == "ask":
            # Surface as ApprovalRequired so the existing pause/decision flow
            # handles it (writes human_decisions + agent_job_events).
            side_effect = "LOCAL_WRITE"
            if spec is not None:
                side_effect = getattr(spec, "side_effect", side_effect) or side_effect
            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, side_effect)

        if spec is not None:
            self._enforce_tool_spec(spec, tool_input)
            timeout = getattr(spec, "timeout_s", None)
        else:
            timeout = None

        if timeout and timeout > 0:
            return self._call_with_deadline(executor, tool_name, tool_input, timeout)
        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)

    def _tool_spec(self, tool_name: str):
        """Resolve a ToolSpec from the kca agent tool_registry, if available."""
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0,
                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"),
            )
            from agent.tool_registry import get_tool  # type: ignore

            return get_tool(tool_name)
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _enforce_tool_spec(self, spec, tool_input: dict) -> None:
        """Cross-check sandbox + isolated_workspace constraints from ToolSpec."""
        sandbox = getattr(spec, "sandbox", None)
        if sandbox == "isolated_workspace":
            # The worker's cwd is the job workspace; tools that resolve paths
            # via ToolExecutor._guard_path already reject traversal. We just
            # confirm the workspace looks set (a None workspace is a bug).
            if not self.workspace:
                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="missing_workspace")
        # ``unsandboxed`` requires explicit "allow" — already gated above; this
        # is a belt-and-braces check.
        if sandbox == "unsandboxed":
            decision = (self.policy.tool_decisions or {}).get(spec.name)
            if decision != "allow":
                raise PolicyViolation(spec.name, decision="unsandboxed_needs_allow")

    def _call_with_deadline(
        self,
        executor: "ToolExecutor",
        tool_name: str,
        tool_input: dict,
        timeout_s: int,
    ) -> str:
        """Best-effort timeout wrapper. ``run_bash`` already times out via
        subprocess; for other tools we just honour the ToolSpec on a wall
        clock and surface a string error if exceeded.
        """
        if tool_name == "run_bash":
            ti = dict(tool_input)
            ti.setdefault("timeout_s", timeout_s)
            return executor.execute(tool_name, ti)
        # In-process tools: run inline; if a future tool turns out to be
        # blocking we can wrap it with signal.alarm/threading.Timer here.
        return executor.execute(tool_name, tool_input)

    def _audit_tool_decision(
        self,
        *,
        tool_name: str,
        decision: str,
        spec,
        tool_input: dict,
    ) -> None:
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0,
                str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent),
            )
            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore

            log_policy_decision(
                tool=tool_name,
                operation=tool_name,
                decision=decision,
                skill_name=self.policy.skill_name,
                mode=self.policy.mode,
                policy_profile=self.policy.policy_profile,
                args=tool_input,
                audit_required=bool(getattr(spec, "audit_required", False))
                if spec is not None
                else False,
                job_id=self.job_id if self.db_url else None,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] {exc}\n")

    def _handle_approval_required(
        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker, start: float
    ) -> WorkerResult:
        """Pause the job and record a decision request.

        M6: when the gating operation is one of KCA_REVIEWER_TRIGGER_OPS,
        first consult the sync reviewer. Reviewer.approve auto-resumes,
        reviewer.reject either escalates to humans (default) or fails the
        job (when KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT=0), and reviewer.abstain
        falls through to the existing human-decisions path.
        """
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # M6 reviewer pre-check
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        reviewer_outcome = self._maybe_consult_reviewer(exc, budget)
        if reviewer_outcome == "approve":
            # Re-execute the gated tool with one-shot bypass.
            return WorkerResult(
                status="reviewer_approved",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="reviewer approved",
                stop_reason="reviewer_approve",
            )
        if reviewer_outcome == "reject_fail":
            self._update_status(
                "failed",
                error="reviewer rejected high-stakes operation",
                budget=budget,
            )
            return WorkerResult(
                status="failed",
                turns_used=budget.turns,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                final_message="",
                stop_reason="reviewer_reject",
            )
        # reviewer_outcome in {None, "reject_escalate", "abstain"} — fall
        # through to human-decisions flow.
        decision_id = None
        if self.db_url:
            try:
                import sys

                sys.path.insert(
                    0,
                    str(
                        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca"
                    ),
                )
                import db as _db

                decision_id = _db.insert_approval_request(
                    decision_type="tool_approval",
                    prompt=f"Worker job {self.job_id} wants to call {exc.tool_name}",
                    options={
                        "approve": "allow this tool call",
                        "deny": "block and stop job",
                    },
                    job_id=self.job_id,
                )
                _db.update_job(
                    self.job_id,
                    status="paused",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
        self._append_event(
            "approval_pause",
            budget.turns,
            event_data={
                "tool": exc.tool_name,
                "operation": exc.tool_name,
                "tool_input": exc.tool_input,
                "side_effect": exc.side_effect,
                "decision_id": decision_id,
            },
        )
        import sys

        print(
            f"JOB PAUSED — run `kca decisions approve --id {decision_id}` to resume",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return WorkerResult(
            status="paused",
            turns_used=budget.turns,
            cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
            duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
            final_message=f"Waiting for approval: decision_id={decision_id}",
            stop_reason="approval_required",
        )

    @classmethod
    def resume(
        cls,
        job_id: str,
        *,
        workspace: Path,
        policy: JobPolicy | None = None,
        db_url: str | None = None,
        dry_run: bool = False,
    ) -> "AgentWorker":
        """Construct an AgentWorker primed from prior agent_job_events.

        Reads the job row + events; reconstructs (turns_used, cost_usd) and
        seeds a one-shot approval allowlist for the paused tool_input so the
        next gate check passes once.
        """
        import sys as _sys

        _sys.path.insert(
            0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
        )
        import db as _db

        job = _db.get_job(job_id)
        events = _db.list_job_events(job_id)
        turns = int(job.get("turns_used") or 0)
        cost = float(job.get("cost_usd") or 0)
        last_pause_input = None
        last_pause_op = None
        # Walk events: the most recent approval_pause defines the next-resume
        # allowlist entry, unless followed by an approval_resume already
        # consumed in a previous resume attempt.
        for ev in events:
            t = ev.get("event_type")
            ed = ev.get("event_data") or {}
            if isinstance(ed, str):
                try:
                    ed = json.loads(ed)
                except Exception:
                    ed = {}
            if t == "approval_pause":
                last_pause_input = ed.get("tool_input")
                last_pause_op = ed.get("operation") or ed.get("tool")
            elif t == "approval_resume":
                # Resume consumed; clear pending allowance.
                last_pause_input = None
                last_pause_op = None
        prompt = job.get("prompt") or ""
        policy = policy or JobPolicy()
        worker = cls(
            job_id=job_id,
            prompt=prompt,
            policy=policy,
            workspace=workspace,
            db_url=db_url,
            dry_run=dry_run,
            resume_state={
                "turns_used": turns,
                "cost_usd": cost,
                "allow_once": {
                    "operation": last_pause_op,
                    "tool_input": last_pause_input,
                }
                if last_pause_op
                else None,
            },
        )
        return worker

    def _maybe_consult_reviewer(
        self, exc: ApprovalRequired, budget: BudgetTracker
    ) -> str | None:
        """Run the sync reviewer for trigger ops; return outcome tag.

        Returns one of:
          None             — reviewer not consulted (op not in trigger set or
                              already reviewed)
          "approve"        — reviewer approved; caller resumes the tool
          "reject_fail"    — reviewer rejected and ESCALATE_REJECT=0
          "reject_escalate"— reviewer rejected, caller should page humans
          "abstain"        — reviewer abstained, caller should page humans
        """
        from src.worker.reviewer import (
            Reviewer,
            ReviewRequest,
            should_consult_reviewer,
            escalate_reject,
        )

        target_op = _resolve_target_op(exc.tool_name)
        if not should_consult_reviewer(target_op):
            return None
        if not self.db_url:
            # No DB → no event trail and no place to record the verdict.
            # The dry-run worker still records the reviewer span via OTEL when
            # T005 wires it up; for now just skip silently.
            return None
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            # Skip if reviewer already ran for (job_id, target_op).
            try:
                existing = _db.find_review_for_op(self.job_id, target_op)
            except Exception:
                existing = None
            if existing is not None:
                return None
            events = []
            try:
                events = _db.list_job_events(self.job_id)
            except Exception:
                events = []
            req = ReviewRequest(
                job_id=self.job_id,
                target_op=target_op,
                tool_name=exc.tool_name,
                tool_input=exc.tool_input,
                final_message=None,
                event_trail=events,
            )
            reviewer = Reviewer(dry_run=self.dry_run)
            verdict = reviewer.review(req)
            try:
                _db.create_review(
                    job_id=self.job_id,
                    reviewer_model=verdict.reviewer_model,
                    verdict=verdict.verdict,
                    target_op=target_op,
                    rationale=verdict.rationale,
                    evidence=verdict.evidence,
                    cost_usd=verdict.cost_usd,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
            if verdict.verdict == "approve":
                self._append_event(
                    "approval_resume",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "source": "reviewer",
                        "verdict": "approve",
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                    },
                )
                return "approve"
            if verdict.verdict == "reject":
                if escalate_reject():
                    self._append_event(
                        "reviewer_reject",
                        budget.turns,
                        event_data={
                            "target_op": target_op,
                            "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                            "escalated": True,
                        },
                    )
                    return "reject_escalate"
                self._append_event(
                    "reviewer_reject",
                    budget.turns,
                    event_data={
                        "target_op": target_op,
                        "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                        "escalated": False,
                    },
                )
                return "reject_fail"
            # abstain → fall through
            self._append_event(
                "reviewer_abstain",
                budget.turns,
                event_data={
                    "target_op": target_op,
                    "rationale": verdict.rationale[:200],
                },
            )
            return "abstain"
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _append_event(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        turn_number: int,
        *,
        input_tokens: int | None = None,
        output_tokens: int | None = None,
        cost_usd: float | None = None,
        event_data: dict | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not self.db_url:
            return
        try:
            import sys

            sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.append_job_event(
                self.job_id,
                event_type,
                turn_number=turn_number,
                input_tokens=input_tokens,
                output_tokens=output_tokens,
                cost_usd=cost_usd,
                event_data=event_data or {},
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _update_status(
        self,
        status: str,
        *,
        error: str | None = None,
        budget: BudgetTracker | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not self.db_url:
            return
        try:
            import datetime
            import sys

            sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.update_job(
                self.job_id,
                status=status,
                error=error,
                turns_used=budget.turns if budget else None,
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd if budget else None,
                finished_at=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc),
            )
        except Exception:
            pass
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as _dt
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_BLOCKED, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect
from _util import warn

import db

_GATE_ENV = "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE"


# ADR-0006 default policy: True = require approval, False = allow.
OPERATION_DEFAULTS = {
    "kaggle_submit": False,
    "kernel_push": False,
    "dataset_upload": True,
    "git_push": False,
    "git_force_push": True,
    "supabase_migrate": True,
    "delete_artifact": True,
    "external_fetch": False,
}


class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
    """Raised when a gated operation lacks approval under the active policy."""

    def __init__(self, operation: str, policy: dict):
        self.operation = operation
        self.policy = policy
        super().__init__(f"ApprovalRequired: {operation}")


def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ApprovalRequired if `policy` (or defaults) gates `operation`.

    KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 remains an emergency CI override.
    """
    gates = (policy or {}).get("approval_gates", {})
    requires = gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS.get(operation, True))
    if requires and not os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV):
        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy or {})


def _gate(side_effect: SideEffect, command_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    if side_effect in (SideEffect.READ_ONLY, SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE):
        return True, None
    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) == "1":
        warn(f"REMOTE OPERATION: kaggle {command_name} — {_GATE_ENV} is set")
        return True, None
    return False, f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human approval"


def _record_approval(command_name: str, options: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Insert a pending human_decisions row. Returns (approval_id, warning).

    Best-effort: DB failures never block the refusal path. Caller emits the
    blocked envelope regardless.
    """
    args_summary = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in options.items() if v is not None)
    prompt = f"Approve Kaggle {command_name} ({args_summary or 'no args'})"
    try:
        approval_id = db.insert_approval_request(
            decision_type=f"kaggle.{command_name}",
            prompt=prompt,
            options=options,
        )
        return approval_id, None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"approval recording failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"


def _emit_blocked(
    command_name: str,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
    reason: str,
    options: dict | None = None,
) -> int:
    payload = {
        "ok": False,
        "error": reason,
        "command": f"kaggle {command_name}",
        "side_effect": side_effect.value,
    }
    # Best-effort: record the attempt in human_decisions.
    if options is not None:
        approval_id, warning = _record_approval(command_name, options)
        if approval_id:
            payload["approval_request_id"] = approval_id
            payload["approval_recorded"] = True
        else:
            payload["approval_recorded"] = False
            if warning:
                payload["approval_warning"] = warning
                warn(warning)
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_BLOCKED


def _emit_stub(
    command_name: str, side_effect: SideEffect, extra: dict | None = None
) -> int:
    out = {
        "ok": True,
        "stub": True,
        "command": f"kaggle {command_name}",
        "side_effect": side_effect.value,
    }
    if extra:
        out.update(extra)
    print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_OK


def _emit_json(payload: dict) -> int:
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_OK if payload.get("ok") else EXIT_RUNTIME


def _policy_from_env() -> dict:
    """Load a JSON policy blob from KCA_POLICY env if present; else empty."""
    raw = os.environ.get("KCA_POLICY")
    if not raw:
        return {}
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}


def cmd_submit(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.SUBMISSION
    competition = args.competition
    file_path = args.file
    message = args.message or "kca agent submission"

    if not os.environ.get("KAGGLE_USERNAME"):
        return _emit_json(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "KAGGLE_USERNAME not set; cannot submit",
                "competition": competition,
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
    if not os.environ.get("KAGGLE_KEY"):
        return _emit_json(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "KAGGLE_KEY not set; cannot submit",
                "competition": competition,
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )

    try:
        _check_approval_gate("kaggle_submit", _policy_from_env())
    except ApprovalRequired:
        return _emit_blocked(
            "submit",
            se,
            "ApprovalRequired: kaggle_submit",
            options={"competition": competition, "file": file_path, "message": message},
        )

    proc = subprocess.run(
        [

        ],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return _emit_json(
        {
            "ok": proc.returncode == 0,
            "competition": competition,
            "file": file_path,
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "stdout": proc.stdout,
            "stderr": proc.stderr,
```
